name: Question 11
problem: Calculate the asymptotes of the hyperbola $16{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}-64x-2y+47=0.$
worked_solution:
To rewrite the equation of the hyperbola in standard form, we need to group the $x$ and $y$ terms and complete the squares, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}16{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}-64x-2y+47 & =0 \\ (16{x}^{2}-64x)+(-{y}^{2}-2y)+47 & =0 \\ 16[{x}^{2}-4x]-[{y}^{2}+2y]+47 & =0 \\ 16[(x-2)^{2}-4]-[(y+1)^{2}-1]+47 & =0 \\ 16(x-2)^{2}-64-(y+1)^{2}+1+47 & =0 \\ 16(x-2)^{2}-(y+1)^{2} & =64-1-47 \\ 16(x-2)^{2}-(y+1)^{2} & =16 \\ \frac{16(x-2)^{2}}{16}-\frac{(y+1)^{2}}{16} & =\frac{16}{16} \\ \frac{(x-2)^{2}}{1}-\frac{(y+1)^{2}}{16} & =1\end{aligned}
$$

The asymptotes of a horizontal hyperbola

$$
\frac{(x-h)^{2}}{{a}^{2}}-\frac{(y-k)^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1
$$

are given by 

$$
y-k=\pm \frac{b}{a}(x-h).
$$

In our case, we have 

$$
h=2,\,k=-1,\,a=\sqrt{1}=1,\,b=\sqrt{16}=4.
$$

Therefore, the asymptotes of the hyperbola are

$$
\begin{aligned}y+1 & =\pm \frac{4}{1}(x-2) \\  & =\pm 4(x-2).\end{aligned}
$$

Question 11
?

Calculate the asymptotes of the hyperbola 16x2−y2−64x−2y+47=0.

a
y+1=±4(x−2)
b
y−2=(x−2)
c
y−1=±14(x+2)
d
y−2=±14(x+1)
e
y−4=±2(x+1)
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

To rewrite the equation of the hyperbola in standard form, we need to group the x and y terms and complete the squares, as follows:

16x2−y2−64x−2y+47=0(16x2−64x)+(−y2−2y)+47=016[x2−4x]−[y2+2y]+47=016[(x−2)2−4]−[(y+1)2−1]+47=016(x−2)2−64−(y+1)2+1+47=016(x−2)2−(y+1)2=64−1−4716(x−2)2−(y+1)2=1616(x−2)216−(y+1)216=1616(x−2)21−(y+1)216=1

The asymptotes of a horizontal hyperbola

(x−h)2a2−(y−k)2b2=1

are given by

y−k=±ba(x−h).

In our case, we have

h=2,k=−1,a=1=1,b=16=4.

Therefore, the asymptotes of the hyperbola are

y+1=±41(x−2)=±4(x−2).
